<!-- Files-and-Folders.md -->

# Files and folders

## On your machine

`~/.compost`, or `$COMPOST_HOME`:

```
~/.compost/
├── compost-manager.yaml    manager key; copy it (or use `init --key`) to manage the same servers elsewhere
├── servers.yaml            servers from `server define`
├── config.yaml             preferences from `compost config`
├── current_context         server name from `connect`
└── ssh/                    shared SSH connection sockets
```

## In an app repository

```
myapp/
├── docker-compose.yaml                compose file, never changed by compost
├── compost.yaml                       how to deploy; commit
├── .compost.secrets.example.yaml      example overlay from `app generate`; commit
├── .compost-staging.yaml              overlay with secrets; don't commit
├── .compostignore                     not uploaded (gitignore syntax)
├── .claude/skills/compost/            Agent Skill from `compost agent skill`, if you install it there
└── …
```

Not uploaded with the sources: `.git/`, files given with `-f`, `.compost-*.yaml`, `.compost.*.yaml` and `.compostignore` patterns. With `deployment.source_dir`, the uploaded folder is that one instead, and `compost.yaml` can live in a separate deployment repository ([Applications](Applications.md#sources-in-another-folder)).

## In an infrastructure folder

```
infra/
├── compost-server.yaml                    shared apps; commit
├── compost-server.prod.yaml               overrides for the real server; commit
├── .compost-server.secrets.example.yaml   commit
└── .compost-server.secrets.yaml           secrets; don't commit
```

## On the server

`~/.compost-server` of the server user, or `server_home` from `servers.yaml`. compost writes only here and to Docker, and, for [scheduled backups](Backup-and-Restore.md#scheduled-backups), one line in the server user's crontab, between `# compost: scheduled backups of <folder>` and `# compost: end of <folder>`.

```
~/.compost-server/
├── manager_key                       key of the compost installation managing this server
├── compost-server.yaml               effective server config, without secrets
├── state.yaml                        status of shared apps and instances, last runs of scheduled backups, notified alerts
├── lock/                             exists while a command changes the server
├── bin/compost                       compost itself, for scheduled backups
├── logs/backup.log                   output of scheduled backups and notifications
├── tmp/                              short-lived files, e.g. client credentials for external databases, archives on their way to or from an S3 target
├── backups/                          archives of the `server` backup target; a profile's are named `<instance or server>-<profile>-<time>…`
├── secrets/apps/<app>/<prefix>.yaml  overlay stored by `secret deploy` or `app deploy --secret`
├── secrets/server.yaml               shared apps' secrets stored by `server deploy --secret`
├── shared/
│   ├── ingress/caddy-main/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── compose.override.yaml     from its `monitoring`, if set
│   │   ├── conf/Caddyfile
│   │   ├── conf/sites/<instance>-<entry>.caddy
│   │   ├── conf/custom/<site>.caddy  `sites` of compost-server.yaml
│   │   ├── data/                     certificates
│   │   ├── config/
│   │   ├── build/Dockerfile          caddysecurebuild: the image built on the server
│   │   ├── conf/crowdsec/            caddysecurebuild: the CrowdSec agent's log sources, ban profile, whitelist
│   │   ├── logs/access.log           caddysecurebuild: access log of every site, read by CrowdSec
│   │   └── secrets/crowdsec.env      caddysecurebuild: key of the bouncer in Caddy
│   ├── database/postgres18/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── data/                     PGDATA
│   │   └── secrets/postgres.env      root password
│   ├── oidc/keycloak/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── compose.override.yaml     networks and database settings from its links
│   │   └── secrets/keycloak.env      admin user and password
│   ├── keyvalue/valkey/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── conf/server.conf, conf/users.acl   settings; users of the links (password hashes)
│   │   ├── data/                     snapshot and append-only files
│   │   └── secrets/password.env      password of the `default` user
│   ├── storage/storage/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── garage.toml               Garage's settings, with its RPC secret and admin token
│   │   ├── meta/, data/              metadata and objects
│   │   └── secrets/garage.env        the RPC secret and admin token, kept across deploys
│   ├── communication/ops-chat/       a communication app: no compose project
│   │   ├── build/                    Dockerfile and script of compost's image, unless `image` is set
│   │   ├── image                     the image to run
│   │   └── secrets/communication.env the channel's settings and credentials
│   ├── workflow/temporal/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml              schema, server, admin and ui
│   │   ├── compose.override.yaml     networks and settings from its links (databases, ingress, oidc)
│   │   ├── schema.sh                 creates or updates Temporal's tables
│   │   ├── cluster.env               the shard count, fixed by the first deploy
│   │   └── dynamicconfig/docker.yaml `dynamic_config`
│   └── monitoring/monitoring/
│       ├── compose.yaml              openobserve and collector
│       ├── compose.override.yaml     ingress network, if `url` is set
│       ├── data/                     OpenObserve's data
│       ├── collector/config.yaml
│       ├── collector/targets/<instance>-<entry>.yaml   metrics endpoints of a link
│       └── secrets/                  openobserve.env, collector.env: root email and password
├── connectors/                       link records, one per instance and entry
│   ├── ingress/caddy-main/<instance>-<entry>.yaml
│   ├── database/postgres18/root-connector.yaml, <instance>-<entry>.yaml
│   │                                 (for an external database: how to reach it, and root credentials)
│   ├── oidc/keycloak/root-connector.yaml, <instance>-<entry>.yaml
│   ├── workflow/temporal/<instance>-<entry>.yaml   the link's namespace and retention
│   └── monitoring/monitoring/root-connector.yaml, <instance>-<entry>.yaml
│                                     (root-connector.yaml: URL and root login)
└── apps/<app>/<prefix>/
    ├── sources/                      uploaded files; .compost/ holds the compose_overrides
    ├── compose/compost.override.yaml networks and variables added to your services
    ├── compost.yaml                  effective app config, without secrets
    ├── compost-env.yaml              shared apps this instance uses; links still to remove
    └── releases/<n>/                 a release for `app rollback`: sources/, compost.yaml, release.yaml (time, images)
```

Files with secrets (`secrets/`, connector records of databases and OIDC, `root-connector.yaml` files, `compost.override.yaml`) have mode `0600`, their folders `0700`. Only compost writes `state.yaml`; a compost that does not know its layout (its `schema`) refuses to use it and asks to be upgraded.

## Docker names

| Object | Name |
|---|---|
| Instance compose project | `<app>-<prefix>`, e.g. `myapp-staging` |
| Shared app compose project | `compost-<kind>-<name>`, e.g. `compost-database-postgres18` |
| Shared app compose service | `compost-shared-<name>`, e.g. `compost-shared-postgres18`; OpenObserve's collector is `compost-shared-<name>-collector`, Temporal's other services `compost-shared-<name>-schema`, `-admin` and `-ui`, the CrowdSec agent of a `caddysecurebuild` ingress `compost-shared-<name>-crowdsec`. Compose makes the service name a host name on every network the container joins, so it is unique on purpose: an app's own `postgres` service stays `postgres` |
| Shared app container | `compost-<kind>-<name>`, like its project, e.g. `compost-database-postgres18`; OpenObserve's collector is `compost-monitoring-<name>-collector`, Temporal's admin tools `compost-workflow-<name>-admin`, a CrowdSec agent `compost-ingress-<name>-crowdsec` |
| Built image | `compost-caddysecurebuild-<name>:<hash>` of a `caddysecurebuild` ingress; `compost-communication:<hash>` of communication apps |
| Release image | `compost-release/<app>-<prefix>:<n>-<service>`: the image a service ran in release `<n>`, kept for `app rollback` |
| Volumes | `compost-ingress-<name>_crowdsec-data` and `_crowdsec-config`: state of a CrowdSec agent |
| Ingress network | `compost-ingress`; a `caddysecurebuild` ingress also has `compost-ingress-<name>_crowdsec`, which only Caddy and its CrowdSec agent join |
| Database network | `compost-db-<name>`; the database's host name is `<name>` |
| Key-value network | `compost-kv-<name>`; host name `<name>` |
| Storage network | `compost-storage-<name>`; host name `<name>` |
| OIDC network | `compost-oidc-<name>`; host name `<name>` |
| Workflow network | `compost-wf-<name>`; host name `<name>` |
| Monitoring network | `compost-monitoring-<name>`; the collector's host name is `<name>` |
| A service's name on the ingress and monitoring networks | `<app>-<prefix>-<service>`; for a shared app its service name, `compost-shared-<name>` |

So you can use plain Docker commands:

```sh
docker compose -p myapp-staging logs -f backend
docker compose -p compost-database-postgres18 exec compost-shared-postgres18 psql -U postgres
docker exec -it compost-database-postgres18 psql -U postgres
```

From your machine, `compost app logs` and `compost server logs` show the same output without logging in to the server (see [Logs](Applications.md#logs)).

---

<!-- CLI-Reference.md -->

# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs.sh from the help texts in src/cli; run `just docs` instead of editing. -->

The `--help` of every command. Guides: [Applications](Applications.md), [Servers and shared apps](Servers-and-Shared-Apps.md), [Backup and restore](Backup-and-Restore.md).

Exit codes: `0` OK · `1` unexpected error · `2` invalid local config or usage · `3` server not ready or a server-side check failed · `4` deployed, but not healthy · `130` interrupted with Ctrl-C.

## `compost`

```text
Manage docker-based server deployments

Usage: compost [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init        Create the local compost home with a new (or the given) manager key
  server      Define, inspect and deploy servers
  connect     Use <NAME> as the default server for following commands
  disconnect  Forget the default server
  app         Deploy and inspect user applications
  connector   Inspect links between applications and shared apps
  backup      Run backup profiles, list and prune backups
  notify      Send notifications through the server's communication apps
  secret      Store application secrets on the server for `app deploy`
  config      Set and show preferences, e.g. `deploy.apply`
  agent       Documentation for AI agents: llms.txt, llms-full.txt and an Agent Skill
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version
```

## `compost init`

```text
Create the local compost home with a new (or the given) manager key

Usage: compost init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --key <KEY>            Use this manager key (a UUID) instead of a new one, e.g. to manage the servers of another compost installation from this machine
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --force                Replace the manager key of an initialized home
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost server`

```text
Define, inspect and deploy servers

Usage: compost server [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  generate  Write starter compost-server.yaml, compost-server.prod.yaml and a secrets example
  define    Add or replace a server in the local configuration
  list      List defined servers
  state     Check and display server state
  deploy    Deploy shared applications from compost-server.yaml
  backup    Back up shared applications (data, configuration and secrets)
  restore   Restore shared applications from a server backup
  logs      Show the output of a shared application's containers
  prune     Show disk usage, then remove images no container uses (except those kept for `app rollback`), dangling images and the build cache
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost server generate`

```text
Write starter compost-server.yaml, compost-server.prod.yaml and a secrets example

Usage: compost server generate [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --list                 List the shared app types that can be generated
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --with <WITH>          Shared app types to include, e.g. `caddy,postgres` (asked when not given)
      --force                Overwrite existing files
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost server define`

```text
Add or replace a server in the local configuration

Usage: compost server define [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Server name used in other commands

Options:
      --address <ADDRESS>              Host name or IP address (SSH)
  -s, --server <SERVER>                Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --user <USER>                    SSH user [default: compostuser]
  -v, --verbose                        Print every command run on the server
      --port <PORT>                    SSH port
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>            SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
      --identity-file <IDENTITY_FILE>  SSH private key (default: ssh config, agent, ~/.ssh/id_*)
      --server-home <SERVER_HOME>      compost directory on the server (default ~/.compost-server)
      --local                          Manage this machine instead of a remote server
      --force                          Replace an existing server with the same name
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

## `compost server deploy`

```text
Deploy shared applications from compost-server.yaml

Usage: compost server deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply                Also start or restart services (default: `deploy.apply`, see `compost config`)
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --no-apply             Only upload files, even when `deploy.apply` is set
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
  -f, --file <FILES>         Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
      --dry-run              Validate and show what would change on the server, without changing it
      --diff                 With --dry-run: also show the changed lines of files without secrets
      --force-unlock         Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
      --pull                 Pull images again, even when their tags did not change, and build images that compost builds on newer base images (needs `--apply`)
      --recreate             Recreate every container, even unchanged ones; data in volumes is kept (needs `--apply`)
      --secret <FILE>        Overlay with secrets (e.g. .compost-server.secrets.yaml) to store on the server and deploy with, replacing the stored one; later deploys use it without the file
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost server backup`

```text
Back up shared applications (data, configuration and secrets)

Usage: compost server backup [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --shared <SHARED>      Only this shared app (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --profile <NAME>       Backup profile from `backup.profiles`: what to save, where, and how many archives to keep. The other options override it
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --format <FORMAT>      `compost` (restorable archive, the default) or `raw` (plain files: one as is, several as tar.gz) [possible values: compost, raw]
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>      Output file or folder (with a target on the server: a file name in its folder)
      --target <TARGET>      Where to write: `local`, `server` or a name from `backup.targets` (default: the profile's, the app's `backup.target`, then the server's, else local)
      --force-unlock         Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost server restore`

```text
Restore shared applications from a server backup

Usage: compost server restore [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVE>

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVE>  Archive written by `compost server backup` (with `--source server`: a file in the server's backup folder)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --shared <SHARED>      Only this shared app (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --source <TARGET>      Where the archive is: `local`, `server` or a name from `backup.targets` (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
      --yes                  Do not ask for confirmation
      --force-unlock         Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost server logs`

```text
Show the output of a shared application's containers

Usage: compost server logs [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Shared app, as in compost-server.yaml, e.g. `caddy-main` (`<kind>/<name>` if two kinds use the name)

Options:
      --follow               Keep streaming new output until Ctrl-C
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --tail <TAIL>          Lines to show from the end of each container's output, or `all` [default: 100]
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --since <SINCE>        Only output since this time: a duration like `10m` or a time like `2026-10-17T12:00:00`
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
      --timestamps           Show the time of every line
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost app`

```text
Deploy and inspect user applications

Usage: compost app [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  generate  Write a starter compost.yaml and .compost.secrets.example.yaml from the compose file
  list      List the application instances deployed on the server
  deploy    Deploy the application instance described by the given files
  state     Show the state of an application instance
  logs      Show the output of an application instance's containers
  exec      Run a command in a service's running container, e.g. a shell
  run       Run a command in a new one-off container of a service, e.g. a migration
  remove    Remove an application instance
  backup    Back up an application instance (or all of them)
  restore   Restore an application instance from a compost backup
  releases  List the releases of an application instance kept for rollback
  rollback  Deploy an earlier release of an application instance again, with the images it ran
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost app deploy`

```text
Deploy the application instance described by the given files

Usage: compost app deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply                Also start or restart services (default: `deploy.apply`, see `compost config`)
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --no-apply             Only upload files, even when `deploy.apply` is set
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
  -f, --file <FILES>         Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
      --dry-run              Validate and show what would change on the server, without changing it
      --diff                 With --dry-run: also show the changed lines of files without secrets
      --force-unlock         Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
      --pull                 Pull images again, even when their tags did not change, and build images that compost builds on newer base images (needs `--apply`)
      --recreate             Recreate every container, even unchanged ones; data in volumes is kept (needs `--apply`)
      --prefix <PREFIX>      Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
      --purge <PURGE>        Also delete the data of links dropped from the config, for these kinds, e.g. `--purge database`
      --secret <FILE>        Overlay with secrets (e.g. .compost.secrets.yaml) to store on the server and deploy with, replacing the stored one; later deploys use it without the file
      --backup <PROFILE>     With --apply, back up the deployed instance with this profile first (default: `deployment.backup`); a failed backup stops the deploy
      --no-backup            Skip the backup that `deployment.backup` takes before the deploy
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost app run`

```text
Run a command in a new one-off container of a service, e.g. a migration

Usage: compost app run [OPTIONS] --service <SERVICE> [INSTANCE] -- <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]    Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`
  <COMMAND>...  The command and its arguments, after `--`, e.g. `-- sh` or `-- ls -la /data`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>         Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --app <APP>            Application name (instead of config files)
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --prefix <PREFIX>      Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
      --service <SERVICE>    Compose service whose container runs the command
      --no-deps              Don't start the services it depends on (`depends_on`)
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost app remove`

```text
Remove an application instance

Usage: compost app remove [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]  Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>         Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
  -s, --server <SERVER>      Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --app <APP>            Application name (instead of config files)
  -v, --verbose              Print every command run on the server
      --prefix <PREFIX>      Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
      --ssh-key-file <PATH>  SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file` [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]
      --volumes              Also remove the compose project's volumes
      --purge <PURGE>        Delete the instance's data held by these kinds, e.g. `--purge database`
      --yes                  Do not ask for confirmation
      --force-unlock         Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## `compost app backup`

```text
Back up an application instance (or all of them)

Usage: compost app backup [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]
          Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>
          Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)

  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --app <APP>
          Application name (instead of config files)

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --prefix <PREFIX>
          Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)

      --ssh-key-file <PATH>
          SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file`
          
          [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]

      --all
          Back up every instance on the server: into one archive, or with --profile one archive each

      --include <INCLUDE>
          Parts to save (default: the profile's, else links,sources,volumes; only links with --link)

          Possible values:
          - links:   Data and configuration of links (database dumps, ingress sites)
          - sources: Uploaded sources (only the compose file when sources are not uploaded)
          - volumes: Named volumes listed under `backup.volumes`
          - images:  Docker images of the services, as `docker save` writes them

      --link <LINK>
          Only this link: `<entry>` or `<kind>:<entry>` (repeatable)

      --profile <NAME>
          Backup profile from `backup.profiles`: what to save, where, and how many archives to keep. The other options override it

      --format <FORMAT>
          `compost` (restorable archive, the default) or `raw` (plain files: one as is, several as tar.gz)
          
          [possible values: compost, raw]

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output file or folder (with a target on the server: a file name in its folder)

      --target <TARGET>
          Where to write: `local`, `server` or a name from `backup.targets` (default: the profile's, the app's `backup.target`, then the server's, else local)

      --stop
          Stop every service while volumes are copied, for a consistent copy (default: those in `backup.stop`)

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost app restore`

```text
Restore an application instance from a compost backup

Usage: compost app restore [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVE>

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVE>
          Archive written by `compost app backup` (with `--source server`: a file in the server's backup folder)

Options:
      --instance <INSTANCE>
          Instance in the archive, e.g. `myapp-staging` (needed when it has several)

  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --all
          Restore every instance in the archive

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --prefix <PREFIX>
          Restore under this prefix, e.g. to make a copy

      --ssh-key-file <PATH>
          SSH private key for this command, instead of the server's `identity_file`
          
          [env: COMPOST_SSH_KEY_FILE=]

  -f, --file <FILES>
          Overlays merged over the archived config, e.g. other domains (repeatable or comma-separated)

      --include <INCLUDE>
          Parts to restore (default: all in the archive; only links with --link). Without `sources`, data is loaded into the deployed instance

          Possible values:
          - links:   Data and configuration of links (database dumps, ingress sites)
          - sources: Uploaded sources (only the compose file when sources are not uploaded)
          - volumes: Named volumes listed under `backup.volumes`
          - images:  Docker images of the services, as `docker save` writes them

      --link <LINK>
          Only this link: `<entry>` or `<kind>:<entry>` (repeatable)

      --source <TARGET>
          Where the archive is: `local`, `server` or a name from `backup.targets` (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

      --replace
          Overwrite databases and volumes that already hold data

      --yes
          Do not ask for confirmation

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- AI-Agents.md -->

# AI agents

compost's documentation also comes in forms that AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and others) read well. All of them are made from these wiki pages, so they say the same, and each release carries the ones of its version.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `llms.txt` | What compost is and a list of these pages with links, as [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) describes |
| `llms-full.txt` | Every page in one file, to give an agent the whole documentation at once |
| Agent Skill `compost` | `SKILL.md` (concepts, workflows, safety rules, which page to read for what) and these pages in `references/` |

The skill tells the agent to run `--dry-run` before deploying, and to ask you before `--apply`, removals, restores and changes to stored secrets. It never adds `--yes` on its own, and never commits or prints overlays with passwords.

## From the compost binary

The installed compost carries the files of its own version, and needs no compost home or server for them:

```sh
compost agent skill                          # writes .claude/skills/compost/ in the current folder
compost agent skill --dir ~/.claude/skills   # for all your projects
compost agent skill --dir .agents/skills     # for agents that read skills from there
compost agent llms                           # print llms.txt
compost agent llms --full                    # print llms-full.txt
```

`agent skill` replaces the `compost` skill in that folder, so run it again after updating compost. It refuses to overwrite a `compost/SKILL.md` that isn't compost's skill. You can commit the skill to your app or infrastructure repository so everyone's agent gets it.

## From a release

Every [release](https://github.com/devorgpl/compost/releases) has `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `compost-skill-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz`, listed in its `SHA256SUMS`. The archive holds the `compost` skill folder:

```sh
tar -xzf compost-skill-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz -C ~/.claude/skills
```

## From the repository

[`docs/agents`](https://github.com/devorgpl/compost/tree/master/docs/agents) holds the same files for master, which may describe features not released yet. An agent can fetch [`llms.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devorgpl/compost/master/docs/agents/llms.txt) or [`llms-full.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devorgpl/compost/master/docs/agents/llms-full.txt) from there.
